profile.summary: Orthrus is a family of RNA foundation models that turn a full mature mRNA transcript into an embedding. It was pretrained so that splice isoforms of the same gene, and transcripts of orthologous genes across mammals, get similar embeddings. The embeddings are used, directly or after fine-tuning, to predict mRNA properties such as RNA half-life and ribosome load.

summary_quotes.text: Here, we introduce Orthrus, a Mamba-based mature RNA foundation model pre-trained using a novel self-supervised contrastive learning objective with biological augmentations.

Orthrus is trained by maximizing embedding similarity between curated pairs of RNA transcripts, where pairs are formed from splice isoforms of 10 model organisms and transcripts from orthologous genes in 400+ mammalian species from the Zoonomia Project.
which is crucial for accurate mRNA property prediction such as RNA half-life, ribosome load, and exon junction detection

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Orthrus uses a Mamba encoder, a state-space model whose memory grows linearly with sequence length, so it can read whole mRNAs. The input is a per-base track matrix: four one-hot nucleotide tracks, plus in the 6-track models a coding sequence track (1 at the first base of each codon) and a splice track (1 at the last base of each exon). Pretraining is contrastive: the model maximises embedding similarity between pairs of transcripts formed from splice isoforms and orthologues. One released checkpoint adds a masked language modelling objective. The model returns a mean-pooled embedding per transcript, or per-position hidden states.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The model card lists four checkpoints used in the Nature Methods publication: orthrus-4-track, orthrus-6-track and orthrus-mlm-6-track (embedding size 512) and orthrus-small-6-track (embedding size 256), all under antichronology on Hugging Face. Three pre-publication checkpoints sit under quietflamingo. The GitHub README still describes the earlier 4-track base and 6-track large models loaded from local Lightning checkpoint files. A result should name the Hugging Face repository and its revision; this page read orthrus-4-track at revision 1326c689 and orthrus-6-track at revision 4994263c.

facts.value: Mamba state-space encoder. The orthrus-6-track configuration gives model dimension 512 and 6 layers, with 6 input tracks.

quotes.text: It uses a Mamba encoder backbone, a variant of state-space models specifically designed for long-sequence data, such as RNA.

facts.value: A full spliced mature RNA sequence, one-hot encoded (4 tracks, U treated as T), plus coding sequence and splice-site tracks for the 6-track models.

run_guide.summary: Create a CUDA Python environment, load the orthrus-4-track checkpoint from Hugging Face and compute a pooled embedding for a short mRNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 in a mamba or conda environment, as the model card recommends.
A CUDA GPU: the Mamba kernels require CUDA. GPU type and memory are not stated.
Code and weights are MIT licensed; the weights are not gated.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
mamba create -n orthrus python=3.10
mamba activate orthrus
steps.explanation: Creates and activates a Python 3.10 environment, as in the model card.

steps.title: Install PyTorch, transformers and the Mamba kernels
steps.shell:
pip install 'torch>=2.2' 'transformers<4.46' 'huggingface_hub>=0.24' safetensors
pip install causal-conv1d==1.2.0.post2 --no-build-isolation --no-cache-dir
pip install mamba-ssm==1.2.0.post1 --no-build-isolation --no-cache-dir
steps.explanation: The model card pins the Mamba kernel versions for the published checkpoints.

steps.title: Load the model and embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    "antichronology/orthrus-4-track",
    trust_remote_code=True,
).to(device).eval()

sequence = (
    "TCATCTGGATTATACATATTTCGCAATGAAAGAGAGGAAGAAAAGGAAGCAGCAAAATATGTGGAGGCCCA"
    "ACAAAAGAGACTAGAAGCCTTATTCACTAAAATTCAGGAGGAATTTGAAGAACATGAAGTTACTTCCTCC"
)
oh = model.seq_to_oh(sequence).unsqueeze(0).to(device)  # (1, L, 4)
lengths = torch.tensor([oh.shape[1]], device=device)

with torch.no_grad():
    emb = model.representation(oh, lengths, channel_last=True)
# emb.shape == (1, D)
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's load and pooled-representation snippets, joined and wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the weights and runs custom model code from the Hugging Face repository (trust_remote_code).

outputs: A pooled embedding tensor of shape (1, D) in memory; the card's comment gives the shape, and the snippet prints nothing.
limitations: These commands were read from the model card and have not been executed by Rewire.
The model card's device line falls back to CPU, but it also states the Mamba backbone requires CUDA.
Using a 6-track checkpoint needs CDS and splice tracks, which the card builds with GenomeKit and a downloaded annotation; that longer example is not reproduced here.

notes: The RNAGym fitness leaderboard row names only 'Orthrus', with no checkpoint or revision. The released dates are the Hugging Face repository creation dates. The pre-publication quietflamingo checkpoints and the legacy antichronology/orthrus repository were not reviewed. bioRxiv returned HTTP 429, so the preprint abstract was read from Europe PMC instead. The paper was later published in Nature Methods (DOI 10.1038/s41592-026-03064-3, per the model card citation); that version was not read.
